# WebSocket reference

<!-- Generated by `make docs-reference` from `assets/wsapi.json`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every server-pushed broadcast and every client command of the WebSocket
API, generated from `assets/wsapi.json` (catalogue version `2.1`). The envelope,
subscription matching, central scoping and resume rules are described in
[External Client Wire Contract](../external-clients/topic-hierarchy.md);
authentication and connection set-up in
[REST & WebSocket API](../integrations/rest-ws.md).

In a topic, `{name}` placeholders stand for one topic segment. In an
argument list, a type ending in `?` marks an optional argument.

## Broadcasts {#broadcasts}

### `alarm_panel` {#broadcasts-alarm-panel}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alarm.countdown` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmCountdownPayload` | Server-pushed: a running exit/entry delay on an alarm zone ticked (once per second). |
| `alarm.health_changed` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmHealthChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the alarm subsystem's health verdict changed (siren stop-verification, service degradations). |
| `alarm.journal_appended` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmJournalAppendedPayload` | Server-pushed: a new entry was appended to the alarm engine's event journal. Payload carries the entry head; clients needing full detail call GET /alarm/journal. |
| `alarm.notification` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmNotificationPayload` | Server-pushed: one enrolled notification output fired for an alarm — a deliberate, per-zone, mode-filtered notification signal (one-shot at fire time, never cancelled by a later silence). |
| `alarm.panel_changed` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmPanelChangedPayload` | Alarm-control-panel entity projection changed (state, availability, code policy, identity, or removal). |
| `alarm.readiness_changed` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmReadinessChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: an alarm zone's per-mode arm-readiness was recomputed (docs/alarm-concept.md §6.3). Carries the full per-mode map, not a delta. |
| `alarm.reminder` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmReminderPayload` | Server-pushed: an arm schedule elapsed with auto-arm off while the zone was not in the scheduled mode, so the engine notifies rather than arming (docs/alarm-concept.md §15 row 19). |
| `alarm.state_changed` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmStateChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: an alarm zone's arm-state-machine transitioned (docs/alarm-concept.md §5). |
| `alarm.triggered` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmTriggeredPayload` | Server-pushed: an alarm zone entered `triggered` and an incident was opened (or re-adopted after a restart / reconnect). |
| `alarm.walktest_progress` | `alarm.panel` | `AlarmWalkTestProgressPayload` | Server-pushed: a walk-test session on an alarm zone recorded a sensor activation. |

### `central` {#broadcasts-central}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `central.features_changed` | `central.{name}.features` | `CentralFeaturesChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the set of features a central offers changed (its first bring-up resolved the system, or the daemon's credential gained or lost a scope). Carries the complete current set keyed by feature, each with available, reason and scope, so the UI shows or hides what the central can do without polling /system/ccu. |
| `central.readiness_changed` | `central.{name}.readiness` | `CentralReadinessChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a CentralUnit's readiness-gated southbound bring-up advanced a phase (waiting_for_ccu -&gt; loading_hub -&gt; loading_devices -&gt; ready), pushed live so the UI distinguishes a central still initializing from one that is offline. |
| `central.state_changed` | `central.{name}.state` | `CentralStateChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a CentralUnit transitioned between lifecycle states (CONNECTING, READY, STOPPED, …). |

### `custom_data_point` {#broadcasts-custom-data-point}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom_data_point.state_changed` | `device.{address}.cdps.{name}` | `CustomDataPointStateChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a CCU data-point change observable to a Custom-DP altered the CDP's aggregated state. SPA tiles subscribe to one CDP-scoped topic instead of N per-DP topics. |

### `datapoint` {#broadcasts-datapoint}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `datapoint.optimistic_rolled_back` | `device.{address}.channels.{channel}.data_points.{parameter}` | `OptimisticRollbackPayload` | Server-pushed: an optimistic write was rolled back (CCU never confirmed within TTL, or rejected it). Rides the same data_points topic as datapoint.value_changed — subscribers route by envelope `type`. |
| `datapoint.value_changed` | `device.{address}.channels.{channel}.data_points.{parameter}` | `DataPointValueChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the value of a wire data-point changed on the CCU. One topic per (device, channel, parameter) tuple. Subscribe with `classify:true` to receive inline category / data_point_type on the payload (default off). `value` is the raw CCU wire value; when the data point declares a non-trivial multiplier the payload also carries `display_value`, the same reading expressed in the unit the data point names. It matches the `display_value` on the REST data-point summary, so a client that seeds from REST and updates from here shows one consistent number. NOT filtered by onboarding release state: a device an operator has accepted but not yet released streams values here like any other, because the Config UI needs them to verify the device before releasing it. A consumer that adopts devices must therefore drop these frames for a device whose `released` is false — the state arrives on `device.created` and is lifted by `device.released`, both on the device's lifecycle topic. Filtering the device LIST alone is not enough. |

### `devices` {#broadcasts-devices}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device.availability_changed` | `device.{address}.lifecycle` | `DeviceAvailabilityChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a device's effective reachability flipped (its interface lost the connection, or the device itself reported UNREACH / STICKY_UNREACH). Rides the same device.{address}.lifecycle topic as device.created — subscribers route by envelope `type`. |
| `device.created` | `device.{address}.lifecycle` | `DeviceCreatedPayload` | Server-pushed: a device the daemon did not know before was observed in the registry. Not sent for the full-inventory announcement the CCU repeats after every reconnect — only an address the device registry does not already hold is announced, so a client may treat this frame as a genuine arrival rather than filtering the fleet out of it. The `source` field says which kind: NEW is a pairing, REFRESH a factory-reset re-pair (the device kept its address but rebuilt its channels), MANUAL an operator accepting a device out of the deferred-creation inbox, CACHE a device restored from the persisted description cache at boot. |
| `device.metadata_changed` | `device.{address}.lifecycle` | `DeviceMetadataChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a device or one of its channels was renamed, or its room / function assignment changed. Rides the same device.{address}.lifecycle topic as device.created — subscribers route by envelope `type`. Address is always the DEVICE address even when a channel changed, because a client materialises a device's name and area as one unit and has to re-read the whole device to stay consistent. |
| `device.refreshed` | `device.{address}.lifecycle` | `DeviceRefreshedPayload` | Server-pushed: a device's VALUES data was observed from the CCU — a pushed event or an active read (boot seed, periodic sweep, operator refresh), whether or not any value changed. Throttled by the daemon to one frame per device per two-second window, so `refreshed_at` may trail the device's exact latest observation by up to that window; the REST device summary's `availability.LastRefreshed` carries the exact value. Rides the same device.{address}.lifecycle topic as device.created — subscribers route by envelope `type`. |
| `device.released` | `device.{address}.lifecycle` | `DeviceReleasedPayload` | Server-pushed: an operator finished onboarding a device — it stops being withheld from the ecosystems (MQTT and therefore Home Assistant, the Matter bridge, outbound webhooks) and may now be adopted by a consumer of this API too. Rides the same device.{address}.lifecycle topic as device.created; subscribers route by envelope `type`. A broadcast rather than a reply, because the consumer that needs it is precisely the one that was already connected and filtered the device out on its device.created frame: without this push it would never learn the device became adoptable. NOTE: this API does not withhold an unreleased device — the Config UI has to see it to configure it — so a consumer that adopts devices filters on the `released` field of device.created and this frame lifts that filter. |
| `device.removed` | `device.{address}.lifecycle` | `DeviceRemovedPayload` | Server-pushed: the CCU reported a device deletion. The same topic carries device.created — subscribers route by envelope `type`. |
| `device.trigger` | `device.{address}.channels.{channel}.trigger` | `DeviceTriggerPayload` | Server-pushed: a non-state device event fired (keypress, impulse, device error) — one topic per (device, channel). Payload event_type / parameter disambiguate which trigger fired. Distinct from datapoint.value_changed. |

### `hub` {#broadcasts-hub}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `connectivity.changed` | `hub.{central}.connectivity.{interface_id}` | `HubConnectivityChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: per-interface reachability flipped. Topic is scoped per central and per interface id. |
| `hub.alarm_message` | `hub.{central}.alarm_messages` | `HubCountChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the central's alarm-message list changed. Payload carries the current count; clients refresh the full list via GET /alarm-messages. |
| `hub.inbox_changed` | `hub.{central}.inbox` | `HubCountChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the central's inbox (pending pairing candidates) changed. Payload carries the current device count; clients refresh via GET /inbox. |
| `hub.install_mode_changed` | `hub.{central}.install_mode` | `InstallModeChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the CCU install-mode (pairing window) changed state. Topic is scoped per central. |
| `hub.metrics_changed` | `hub.{central}.metrics` | `HubMetricChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a hub metric (system health, connection latency, last-event age) was re-observed. Payload carries the metric name, value and unit. |
| `hub.program_changed` | `hub.{central}.programs.{id}` | `ProgramChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a CCU program's activity flag changed (CCU WebUI toggle or a client write). A program is two controls — the activity flag decides whether it reacts at all, the execution runs it once — and a deactivated program refuses the execution, so `execute_available` travels with the flag. Topic is scoped per central and per program-id. |
| `hub.program_executed` | `hub.{central}.programs.{id}` | `ProgramExecutedPayload` | Server-pushed: a CCU program finished executing (Zentralenprogramm). Topic is scoped per central and per program-id. |
| `hub.service_message` | `hub.{central}.service_messages` | `HubCountChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the central's service-message list changed. Payload carries the current count; clients refresh the full list via GET /service-messages. |
| `hub.system_update_changed` | `hub.{central}.system_update` | `HubSystemUpdateChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the central's CCU firmware-/system-update state changed. Payload carries the current/available firmware, whether an update is available, and whether one is installing; clients can drop their update-status poll loop and refresh via GET /system/update if needed. |
| `hub.sysvar_changed` | `hub.{central}.sysvars.{name}` | `SysvarChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a CCU system variable's value changed. Topic is scoped per central and per sysvar name. |

### `node` {#broadcasts-node}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `node.endpoints_changed` | `node.endpoints_changed` | `NodeEndpointsChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the node reassembled its bridged endpoints (a central became ready, a device was paired or removed, the operator changed the exposure selection or ran the maintenance reassemble). Empty payload; reload GET /api/v1/node/endpoints. |
| `node.exposure_changed` | `node.exposure_changed` | `ExposureEvent` | Server-pushed: the exposure selection changed through PUT /api/v1/node/exposure. Payload: the keys of the changed items (loom's source keys, `central\|address\|channel\|kind\|key`). |
| `node.fabric_added` | `node.fabric_added` | `FabricEvent` | Server-pushed: a controller commissioned the node (post-AddNOC). Payload: the fabric's index, vendor and label — go-fabric-ui's FabricEvent, as its SSE stream (GET /api/v1/node/stream) carries it. |
| `node.fabric_removed` | `node.fabric_removed` | `FabricEvent` | Server-pushed: a fabric was removed — by the operator (DELETE /api/v1/node/fabrics/{index}, the factory reset) or by the controller itself (RemoveFabric). Payload: the fabric index. |
| `node.surface_changed` | `node.surface_changed` | `SurfaceChangedEvent` | Server-pushed: an assembly changed the surface the node serves on one endpoint (its ConfigurationVersion was raised). Payload: the endpoint's key, "" for the root; one event per endpoint. Reload GET /api/v1/node/surface or GET /api/v1/node/endpoints. |
| `node.window_closed` | `node.window_closed` | `WindowEvent` | Server-pushed: the commissioning window closed (commissioned, timed out, revoked). |
| `node.window_opened` | `node.window_opened` | `WindowEvent` | Server-pushed: a commissioning window opened (the operator's POST /api/v1/node/pairing/window, a commissioner's AdministratorCommissioning). The payload carries the discriminator only; the passcode and the pairing codes stay in the admin-gated GET /api/v1/node/pairing response. |

### `schedules` {#broadcasts-schedules}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schedules.changed` | `device.{address}.lifecycle` | `ScheduleChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a channel's week profile changed — written through this daemon, or observed on the CCU. Carries the channel whose schedule moved so a client can re-read it; the profile body is not inlined because a week profile is large and most subscribers only need to invalidate. |

### `security` {#broadcasts-security}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `security.class_changed` | `security.state` | `SecurityClassChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: one hazard or fault class went active or inactive, or its source set changed while it stayed active. |
| `security.fault_changed` | `security.faults` | `SecurityFaultChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: a fault opened, cleared or was acknowledged. Carries the standing fault count after the change. |
| `security.notification` | `security.notifications` | `SecurityNotificationPayload` | Server-pushed: one rendered report, with prose plus the i18n key and args to re-render it. A covert report (duress code, silent panic) rides this broadcast only under alarm.duress_visibility: full — the WebSocket is a local screen surface. |
| `security.state_changed` | `security.state` | `SecurityStateChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the folded severity of the Security & Safety domain changed. Carries the fold only; read GET /security for the detail. |
| `security.zone_changed` | `security.state` | `SecurityZoneChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: one alarm zone's security view changed. Never fires on an installation without an alarm engine, where the domain still reports classes and faults. |

### `system` {#broadcasts-system}

| Name | Topic | Payload | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `addon_update.state_changed` | `system.addon_update` | `AddonUpdateStatus` | Server-pushed: the add-on self-updater changed state (check finished, download/install progressing, failure). Only emitted on platforms where self-update is supported. |
| `daemon_status.changed` | `system.daemon_status` | `DaemonStatusPayload` | Server-pushed: the daemon is stopping. Emitted once during a graceful shutdown, before the servers stop, so a client can tell a stopping daemon apart from its own connection dropping — the distinction MQTT clients get from the broker's last will. A killed daemon cannot send it; detecting that stays the client's own job from its connection state. |
| `pairing.requests_changed` | `system.pairing` | `PairingRequestsChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: the pending client-pairing list changed (a request arrived, was decided, expired or was withdrawn — ADR 0076). Carries only the pending count; the codes and request details stay behind the admin-gated GET /pairing-requests, which the tokens panel fetches on this signal. |
| `system.status_changed` | `system.{central}.status` | `SystemStatusChangedPayload` | Server-pushed: an aggregated system-status transition (component health, callback state, degraded interfaces, …). Topic is scoped per central. |

## Commands {#commands}

### `alarm_panel` {#commands-alarm-panel}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alarm_panel.acknowledge` | `zone_id: string, code: string?` | Acknowledge (clear) a finished incident on an alarm zone. |
| `alarm_panel.arm` | `zone_id: string, mode: string, force: boolean?, skip_delay: boolean?, bypass: array?, code: string?` | Arm an alarm zone. May return synchronously as `armed`, or `arming` while counting down the mode's exit delay. |
| `alarm_panel.codes_create` | `code: object` | Create an alarm code (operator). The cleartext PIN is write-only and hashed before persistence. |
| `alarm_panel.codes_delete` | `id: string` | Delete an alarm code (operator). |
| `alarm_panel.codes_list` |  | List alarm codes (operator). Codes are security material, so even the list is operator-gated; the argon2id hash and cleartext PIN are never returned. |
| `alarm_panel.codes_update` | `id: string, code: object` | Replace an alarm code (operator). An empty PIN keeps the stored hash. |
| `alarm_panel.disarm` | `zone_id: string, code: string?` | Disarm an alarm zone. |
| `alarm_panel.journal` | `zone_id: string?, class: string?, from: string?, to: string?, limit: integer?` | Query the alarm engine's event journal, newest first. |
| `alarm_panel.panels` |  | List the alarm-control-panel entity projections (HA-state view incl. the master panel). |
| `alarm_panel.readiness` | `zone_id: string` | Return the per-mode arm-readiness of an alarm zone. |
| `alarm_panel.silence` | `zone_id: string, code: string?` | Silence the active incident on an alarm zone without disarming. |
| `alarm_panel.silence_all` |  | Silence the active incident on every alarm zone at once. |
| `alarm_panel.state` |  | Return the live status of every alarm zone: state, mode, bypassed sensors, active incident, running countdown, per-mode readiness, and walk-test-active flag. |
| `alarm_panel.walktest_status` | `zone_id: string` | Return the live status of a walk-test session on an alarm zone. |

### `alarms` {#commands-alarms}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alarm_messages.ack` | `id: string, central_name: string?` | Acknowledge (clear) a single alarm message by id. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `alarm_messages.ack_all` | `central_name: string?` | Acknowledge (clear) every active alarm message in one pass. The response carries the number acknowledged. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `alarm_messages.list` | `central_name: string?` | List all active CCU alarm messages. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `service_messages.ack` | `id: string, central_name: string?` | Acknowledge (clear) a single service message by id. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `service_messages.ack_all` | `central_name: string?` | Acknowledge (clear) every quittable service message in one pass. The response carries the number acknowledged. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `service_messages.disable` | `id: string` | Disable (permanently suppress) a single service message by id. Resolves the message's channel + service parameter and suppresses it on the CCU via Interface.suppressServiceMessages until cleared via service_messages.unsuppress. |
| `service_messages.list` | `central_name: string?` | List all active CCU service messages (UNREACH, low-battery, config-pending, etc.). Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `service_messages.suppressed` |  | List the permanently-suppressed service-message channel parameters across every central. Reconciled against each CCU's live Interface.getSuppressedServiceMessages. |
| `service_messages.unsuppress` | `channel: string, parameter: string?, interface: string?` | Clear a permanent service-message suppression. Params: channel (required), parameter (empty = all parameters of the channel), interface (optional, resolved from the stored suppression). |

### `backup` {#commands-backup}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `backup.status` | `central_name: string?` | Return the current status of a running or last-completed CCU backup operation. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `backup.trigger` | `central_name: string?` | Trigger a CCU configuration backup asynchronously. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `backups.trigger` | `central_name: string` | Trigger the create-and-download backup flow for exactly the named central (multi-CCU-correct counterpart to backup.trigger, which always targets the first registered central). Returns the backup/job id. |

| Name | Arguments | Description |

### `ccu` {#commands-ccu}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ccu.cache_clear` | `central: string?, device: string?, interface: string?, kind: string?` | Clear CCU-derivable caches scoped by kind (global/central/interface/device) and trigger a re-pull. Omitting kind defaults to global. Mirrors Python ws_clear_cache (websocket_api.py:1885). |
| `ccu.device_statistics` |  | Return per-interface device statistics: total, unreachable, and firmware-updatable counts plus grand totals. Mirrors Python ws_get_device_statistics (V8-N11). |
| `ccu.get_hub_data` |  | Return service-message count and alarm-message count from hub data points. Mirrors Python ws_get_hub_data (websocket_api.py:2052). |
| `ccu.get_rssi_info` |  | Return per-device RF reception strength (RSSI_DEVICE / RSSI_PEER in dBm), battery state (battery_level, low_battery), and reachability, read from the device model's maintenance channel across every central. Works for HmIP and BidCos alike; only devices that report an RSSI reading are listed. |
| `ccu.get_signal_quality` |  | Return RSSI, reachability, and low-battery state for every known device. Mirrors Python ws_get_signal_quality (websocket_api.py:2158). |
| `ccu.reload_channel_config` | `channel_address: string` | Trigger a CCU-side channel-config reload for the addressed channel: re-pull paramset descriptions (VALUES/MASTER/LINK) + MASTER values and refresh the channel's data points. Mirrors Channel.reload_channel_config (model/device.py:1448). |
| `ccu.reload_device_config` | `device_address: string` | Trigger a CCU-side device-config reload for the addressed device. Mirrors Python ws_panel_reload_device_config (websocket_api.py:2285). Closes parity_audit gap L-7002. |
| `ccu.throttle_stats` |  | Return per-interface command-throttle diagnostics (in_flight, waiting, burst_downgrades, waited_for_burst_slot). Mirrors Python ws_get_command_throttle_stats (V8-N9). |

### `cdp` {#commands-cdp}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cdp.get` | `device: string, name: string` | Return a single custom data point by device address and name. |
| `cdp.invoke` | `device: string, name: string, operation: string, params: object?, priority: string?` | Invoke an operation on a custom data point (turn_on, set_temperature, open, …). Operation arguments use the units and scales a Home Assistant client expects, matching what the custom-data-point STATE reports — not the CCU wire values, which live on the data-point plane. Concretely for a colour light: set_color takes {hue, saturation} with hue in degrees 0..360 and saturation 0..100, the same scale `state.color.s` reports back; the daemon converts to the wire `SATURATION` fraction 0..1 itself. Read and write therefore need no conversion in either direction — scaling `state.color.s` before sending it back is the mistake this note exists to prevent. |
| `cdp.list` | `device: string?` | List all custom data points of all devices (or a single device when 'device' param is supplied). |

### `central` {#commands-central}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `central.connectivity` |  | Report per-interface connectivity details for all configured centrals. |
| `central.create_links` | `address: string?, channel: string?, device_address: string?` | Enable CCU click-event forwarding. Without channel every press-event channel of the device is switched on; with channel (a channel address) only that single channel is touched. Mirrors Python create_central_links. |
| `central.info` |  | Return identity and version information for the connected CCU. |
| `central.links_status` | `address: string?, device_address: string?` | Report whether a device supports central links, how many channels are eligible, and which channels (address, number, eligible) can drive central click events. |
| `central.reconcile` |  | Kick off an ad-hoc reconciliation pass against the CCU device registry. |
| `central.remove_links` | `address: string?, channel: string?, device_address: string?` | Tear down CCU click-event forwarding. Without channel the whole device is switched off; with channel (a channel address) only that single channel is touched. Mirrors Python remove_central_links. |
| `central.system_health` |  | Return a combined system-health snapshot from the CCU's perspective. |

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.reload_channel_config` | `channel_address: string` | Trigger a CCU-side channel-config reload for the addressed channel: re-pull paramset descriptions (VALUES/MASTER/LINK) + MASTER values and refresh the channel's data points. Mirrors Channel.reload_channel_config (model/device.py:1448). |

| `config.session.discard` | `central_name: string?, channel_address: string, paramset_key: string` | Discard all pending changes and close the config session. `channel_address` and `paramset_key` identify the session, the same pair `config.session.open` was called with. |
| `config.session.open` | `central_name: string?, channel_address: string, paramset_key: string` | Open a config session for a channel/paramset pair and return its initial values. |
| `config.session.redo` | `central_name: string?, channel_address: string, paramset_key: string` | Re-apply the most recently undone change in the open config session. `channel_address` and `paramset_key` identify the session, the same pair `config.session.open` was called with. |
| `config.session.save` | `central_name: string?, channel_address: string, paramset_key: string` | Write the pending changes of the open config session to the CCU and close the session. `channel_address` and `paramset_key` identify the session, the same pair `config.session.open` was called with. |
| `config.session.set` | `central_name: string?, channel_address: string, paramset_key: string, parameter: string?, value: any` | Stage a single parameter change into the open config session. |
| `config.session.undo` | `central_name: string?, channel_address: string, paramset_key: string` | Undo the most recent staged change in the open config session. `channel_address` and `paramset_key` identify the session, the same pair `config.session.open` was called with. |

### `devices` {#commands-devices}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `device.install_mode` | `address: string, duration_seconds: integer?` | Put a single device into pairing install-mode for a given duration. |
| `device.rename` | `address: string, name: string, include_channels: boolean?` | Rename a device on the CCU. When include_channels is true every channel is renamed along with the '&lt;name&gt;:&lt;channelNo&gt;' pattern. |
| `device.rename_channel` | `address: string, channel: integer, name: string` | Rename a single channel on the CCU. |
| `device.replace` | `address: string, old_address: string, central: string?` | Swap a paired device for a new one. The CCU migrates direct links, teams and ReGa references; the old device is unpaired. Supported on BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired only. |
| `device.replace_candidates` | `address: string, central: string?` | List the already-paired devices the new (inbox) device may replace. Supported on BidCos-RF and BidCos-Wired only. |
| `device.restore_config` | `address: string` | Re-transmit the centrally stored configuration (all channels' MASTER paramsets + link peerings) to a device after a factory reset. Supported on HmIP-RF and BidCos-RF only. |
| `device.set_channel_functions` | `address: string, channel: integer, functions: array` | Replace a single channel's function (Gewerk) assignments. An empty array clears the set. |
| `device.set_channel_rooms` | `address: string, channel: integer, rooms: array` | Replace a single channel's room assignments. An empty array clears the set. |
| `device.set_team` | `address: string, channel: integer, team: string?` | Assign a channel to a team (e.g. smoke-detector teaming). A null/empty team resets to the channel's default team. BidCos-RF and HmIP-RF only. |
| `device.team_candidates` | `address: string, channel: integer` | List the team channels a channel may be assigned to (same team tag). Supported on BidCos-RF and HmIP-RF only. |
| `device.test` | `address: string` | Run the CCU's per-device communication / function test (radio test frame + ACK). Blocks until complete or the poll window elapses. Radio interfaces only. |
| `devices.export_definition` | `address: string` | Export a device definition as an aiohomematic-compatible zip (device + paramset descriptions, anonymised). Returns model, filename and base64-encoded zip data. |
| `devices.get` | `address: string` | Return the full detail record for a single device by address. |
| `devices.list` |  | Return a summary list of all registered devices sorted by address. |

Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `install_mode.enable` | `interface_id: string, duration_seconds: integer, sgtin: string?, key: string?, central_name: string?` | Open the pairing window for the named interface for a given duration in seconds. Passing sgtin + key (together) requests the keyserver-less HmIP LOCAL teach-in restricted to that one device. `interface_id` accepts either the bare interface type ("HmIP-RF") or the composite `<central>-<interface>` id other commands publish (e.g. devices.list, ccu.get_signal_quality); both resolve to the same pairing window. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `install_mode.search` | `interface_id: string, central_name: string?, central: string?` | Scan the wired bus (BidCos-Wired) for new devices; returns the count found (they join the inbox for acceptance). Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. `central` is accepted as a deprecated alias for `central_name`. |
| `install_mode.status` | `central_name: string?` | Report the current pairing-mode state per interface. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |

### `links` {#commands-links}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `links.activate_paramset` | `receiver_channel_address: string, sender_channel_address: string, long_press: boolean` | Test a direct link at the device: trigger the receiver's LINK paramset for the sender (short or long keypress). Physically actuates the receiver. |
| `links.add` | `sender: string, receiver: string, name: string?, description: string?` | Create a new direct link between a sender and a receiver channel. |
| `links.apply_profile` | `interface_id: string?, sender_channel_address: string, receiver_channel_address: string, profile_id: integer, edit_token: string` | Write a link profile to the LINK paramset of (receiver_channel_address, sender_channel_address). The value set is the profile's fixed constraint values plus the declared defaults of its loose constraints; a loose constraint carrying no default is not written, so the device keeps its current value for it. One consequence is worth knowing before building on this: applying a profile does not guarantee that a later links.get_profiles reports it as the active one, because the parameters that distinguish sibling profiles are frequently loose without a default. This is a configuration write and requires the per-resource edit lock: pass edit_token issued by POST /sessions/edit with key channel:{receiver_channel_address}:LINK:{sender_channel_address}, or the write is rejected with a 'locked' command error. |
| `links.get_form_schema` | `interface_id: string, sender_channel_address: string, receiver_channel_address: string` | Return the form schema (descriptions + current values) for a link paramset between sender and receiver. Mirrors Python ws_get_link_form_schema (websocket_api.py:1057). |
| `links.get_paramset` | `address: string, peer_address: string` | Read the LINK paramset on the given channel keyed by the peer channel address. Mirrors Python ws_get_link_paramset (websocket_api.py:1313). Closes parity_audit gap G-03. |
| `links.get_profiles` | `interface_id: string?, sender_channel_address: string, receiver_channel_address: string, locale: string?` | Return available easymode profiles for a link between sender and receiver channel types. Mirrors Python ws_get_link_profiles (websocket_api.py:1123). Stub until Phase-11. |
| `links.linkable_channels` | `device_address: string` | Return the channels eligible to be linked against a given device. |
| `links.list` | `device_address: string` | List all direct links a device participates in. |
| `links.list_all` | `central: string?` | Global direct-link overview across all centrals (or one when 'central' is set). Each link carries its owning central_name and interface_id. |
| `links.put_paramset` | `address: string, peer_address: string, parameters: object, edit_token: string` | Write values to the LINK paramset on the given channel keyed by the peer channel address. This is a configuration write and is gated behind the same per-resource edit lock as the REST route: pass edit_token issued by POST /sessions/edit with key channel:{address}:LINK:{peer_address}, or the write is rejected with a 'locked' command error. The lock carries the peer because the paramset does — two links on one channel are two resources. |
| `links.remove` | `sender: string, receiver: string` | Delete an existing direct link between a sender and a receiver channel. |
| `links.set_info` | `sender: string, receiver: string, name: string?, description: string?` | Change the name and/or description of an existing direct link. |

### `paramsets` {#commands-paramsets}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `paramset.copy` | `source_channel_address: string, target_channel_address: string, paramset_key: string?` | Copy a paramset (VALUES or MASTER) from a source channel to a target channel by reading + writing the values. Distinct from links.copy (peer-to-peer link-entry copy). Mirrors Python ws_copy_paramset (websocket_api.py:916). Closes parity_audit gap L-7015. |
| `paramset.description` | `channel_address: string, paramset_key: string?, central_name: string?` | Return the parameter descriptors for a channel/paramset pair. |
| `paramset.determine` | `interface_id: string, channel_address: string, parameter_id: string` | Auto-detect a parameter value from the device via determine_parameter. Mirrors Python ws_determine_parameter (websocket_api.py:2556). Stub until Phase-11. |
| `paramset.form_schema` | `address: string, channel_no: integer, paramset: string?, locale: string?, peer: string?` | Return the form schema (descriptions + grouping) for a channel paramset. Mirrors Python ws_get_form_schema (websocket_api.py:252). Closes parity_audit gap G-27. |
| `paramset.get` | `central_name: string?, channel_address: string, paramset_key: string` | Return the current values for a channel/paramset pair. |
| `paramset.put` | `channel_address: string, paramset_key: string, values: object, edit_token: string?` | Write a paramset directly to the CCU without a session (non-transactional from a daemon-session perspective, but atomic on the wire: forwarded as one setParamsetValues XML-RPC call so the CCU applies all values together or none). Returns {written: N} on success; for MASTER the daemon additionally re-reads the stored paramset and reports readback_divergences (every parameter whose stored value differs from the sent one) and readback_error (the post-write read failed; divergences unknown) — an interface process may answer ok and still drop, clamp or coerce a value, so an empty readback_divergences is the only trustworthy full acknowledgement. paramset_key accepts MASTER and VALUES only. LINK is refused here: a LINK paramset belongs to a channel PAIR and is addressed by its partner, which this command carries no argument for — use links.put_paramset with address and peer_address. MASTER writes are configuration changes gated behind the per-resource edit lock: pass edit_token (issued by POST /sessions/edit with key channel:{channel_address}:MASTER) or the write is rejected with a 'locked' command error. VALUES writes are ungated. |

### `programs` {#commands-programs}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `programs.delete` | `id: string, central_name: string?` | Delete a CCU program by id. Removes the program from the CCU (dom.DeleteObject) and drops it from the hub mirror. Admin-gated, mirroring the REST DELETE /programs/{id} route (deletion is irreversible). Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `programs.execute` | `id: string, check_conditions: boolean?, central_name: string?` | Execute a CCU program by id. When `check_conditions` is true the CCU evaluates the program's "if" condition and runs the program only when it is satisfied; when false (the default) the program runs unconditionally. `executed` reports whether the program actually ran — always true for an unconditional run, false for a condition-checked run whose condition was not met. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |
| `programs.list` | `include_internal: boolean?, central_name: string?` | List all CCU programs. Each entry carries optional `channel` / `device_address` fields when the program is associated with a device (device identifier in the program name); absent fields mean the entity belongs on the central hub card. `include_internal` overrides whether internal (Tmp_\*) programs are listed; when omitted the central's include_internal_programs config default applies. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one. |

### `schedules` {#commands-schedules}

| Name | Arguments | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `schedules.active_profile.set` | `channel_address: string, profile_index: integer` | Select the active climate profile (P1..P6) on a thermostat channel. profile_index is 1-based here (P1 is 1); the REST field active_profile_index is 0-based, so add 1 when feeding one to the other. |
| `schedules.climate.copy_profile` | `source_channel_address: string, source_profile: number, target_channel_address: string, target_profile: number` | Copy a single climate profile from a source channel/profile to a target channel/profile. Mirrors Python copy_schedule_profile. |
| `schedules.climate.get` | `channel_address: string` | Read the active climate week-program for a thermostat channel. |
| `schedules.climate.set` | `channel_address: string, profile: object` | Write a climate week-program back to a thermostat channel. The result carries "corrections" only when the stored schedule differs from the submitted one: a time with an hour of 24 and a non-zero minute is stored as 23:55, matching the CCU's own climate editor. Each entry names profile, weekday, period (0-based), field (start_time\|end_time), requested and applied. |
| `schedules.copy` | `source_device_address: string, target_device_address: string` | Copy the whole week schedule from a source device to a target device (channels auto-resolved). Mirrors Python copy_schedule. |
| `schedules.device.active_profile.set` | `device_address: string, profile: string` | Select the active climate profile by name (e.g. P1..P6) on the resolved schedule channel of a device. |
| `schedules.device.get` | `device_address: string` | Read the unified schedule DTO for a device, resolving the correct channel automatically. |
| `schedules.device.set` | `device_address: string, profile: object` | Write a schedule back to the resolved schedule channel of a device. Carries the same optional "corrections" list as schedules.climate.set. |
| `schedules.list_devices` |  | List all devices that expose a weekly schedule (week-profile data point). Mirrors Python ws_list_schedule_devices (websocket_api.py:1491). |
| `schedules.set_enabled` | `device_address: string, enabled: boolean, channel_key: string?` | Enable or disable the weekly program on a device. Mirrors Python ws_set_schedule_enabled (websocket_api.py:1698). Stub until Phase-11. |
